Mobutu Sese Seko. A Congolese military dictator who seized power in 1965 and ruled with authoritarian control and endemic corruption for thirty-two years. His regime, propped up by Cold War geopolitics, became synonymous with kleptocracy, extracting the nation's vast mineral wealth while its people descended into poverty and his personal fortune grew into billions.

Mobutu rose from military ranks to seize power in a coup in November 1965, during the chaos of the Congo Crisis and competing Cold War faction struggles. He renamed the country Zaire from 1971 to 1997 and adopted the grandiose name Sese Seko, meaning the all-powerful warrior, embodying his megalomaniacal vision of supreme national authority. He accumulated a personal fortune estimated at four to five billion dollars through wholesale plunder of state resources, mining revenues, and foreign aid while the national economy collapsed around him.

Mobutu maintained authoritarian control through a secret police called the DGED, suppression of opposition parties, and periodic purges of potential rivals within the military and government. He exploited Cold War rivalries by positioning himself as an anti-communist ally of the United States and Western powers, securing military aid and diplomatic recognition despite his dictatorial rule. While Western governments supported him, his people suffered terribly. He presided over the catastrophic decline of Congo's infrastructure, health, and education systems. Despite enormous mineral wealth, the country became impoverished under his rule—a striking paradox that revealed the nature of kleptocratic extraction.

Mobutu's regime lasted until 1997, when he was forced to flee as rebel forces under Laurent-Désiré Kabila advanced. His regime ended as neighboring countries and regional powers withdrew support, no longer willing to back his increasingly unstable dictatorship. His reign became the textbook case of kleptocratic authoritarianism in post-colonial Africa, demonstrating how Cold War patronage could enable one man's systematic theft of national resources while destroying a nation's institutions. Mobutu Sese Seko remains connected to Zaire, the nation he renamed and destroyed through decades of dictatorship, the Belgian Congo as the colonial legacy he inherited, and the Cold War, the superpower rivalry that enabled his regime through Western support.
